title: Favorite records and a spiritual he recorded
summary: He likes Armstrong and spirituals; talk of his Walking with the King recording being imitated by Ray Bauduc.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Oh yeah, I've been around. I've been around. Something that always interested me, I think you must listen to records more than most musicians.
Well I do, I like the records. You enjoy hearing them. Yeah, I enjoy the records. There's a few here, I'll tell you that.
But anyhow, what are some of your favorite records?

Well I like the jazz records, and I like Lewis, I always did. And at home, like I said, my machine is out of order now, but when I have it I play mostly his records. And spiritual songs, I like that. It was hymns.
What are some of Lewis records that you like, some particular ones?
Well there's none particular, I like all of them. Everything he ever made I like.
Lewis Armstrong is one of them. That's right. And what spirituals do you like?
I like all the spiritual hymns, but they sing. It's good.
Well I know you sing some ones that other people don't sing too much, you know, play too much.
Well yeah. You know what I heard the other morning?
I heard Walking with the King on Arthur Godfrey's problem. Yeah? I wonder if they got that off your record or something.
I think we were the only one that I knew of that recorded it.

Yeah, first and then the Napula man, Ray Baduc, made it later and they got imitated. Did you ever hear that? No. I don't believe we have it here, but Bill Russell has it down. And the guy tries to sing like you and everything. You know them, those two guys used to be with Bob Grosz. Yeah, yeah.

Yeah, Ray Baduc and Napula man. But you know, they're trying to, sound like they're trying to do like you. You do your stuff. So who else do you like on records? Wait a minute, we better stop right now. I think that's the end of The Real. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
